# linlog in the browser

> This page is linlog's prover for linear logic in a web browser, made for people: type a sequent, prove it step by step by clicking, or let linlog's search close a goal, and see the derivation and the proof net drawn. The prover runs in the browser as WebAssembly; the page is static and offers no API to call.

A model that is to decide, check, prove step by step or export sequents does so with linlog's command, `linlog`, or its Rust library, not through this page: the guide below says how, with every command, flag, format and JSON form. This text is under CC BY 4.0, as all of the page's written content.

## Docs

- [linlog's guide for AI models](https://linlog-prover.github.io/linlog/llms.txt): the command and the library in brief, the body of an Agent Skill
- [The full reference](https://linlog-prover.github.io/linlog/llms-full.txt): every command, flag, format, exit status and JSON form, with examples
- [The library's API](https://linlog-prover.github.io/linlog/linlog/): the Rust crate's documentation

## Optional

- [linlog on GitHub](https://github.com/linlog-prover/linlog): the source, README, and the Agent Skill in `skills/linlog/` to copy into an agent's skills
- [Privacy](https://linlog-prover.github.io/privacy/): what the page keeps in the browser and what GitHub logs
